## How it works

- [statement] Krystal documents a Gas Fee Ceiling: if the estimated rebalance cost exceeds the ceiling, Auto-Rebalance does not trigger. This provides a concrete execution-cost gate alongside its slippage controls. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://docs.krystal.app/products/liquidity-management/lp-management/lp-transactions/auto-rebalance · keywords: Rebalance execution swap zap quoting slippage and MEV on Base

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Revert documents sourcing auto-range swaps through the 0x aggregator and applying the configured maximum price impact as the swap execution threshold. This is evidence of an aggregator-based rebalance implementation, not a verified claim that its quoted price is globally optimal. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://docs.revert.finance/revert/auto-range · keywords: Rebalance execution swap zap quoting slippage and MEV on Base

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Uniswap’s routeToRatio configuration separates ratioErrorTolerance from maxIterations; the former bounds ratio error and the latter limits the search, returning an error if the iteration limit is exceeded. These are ratio-search controls, rather than substitutes for swap slippage limits. (low confidence) — https://docs.uniswap.org/sdk/v3/guides/liquidity/swap-and-add · keywords: Rebalance execution swap zap quoting slippage and MEV on Base
- [statement] Uniswap’s v3 Quoter relies on state-changing calls that revert to return quote data; the guide recommends offchain simulation via callStatic rather than an expensive onchain Quoter call. Its quoteExactInputSingle example returns the quoted output amount. (low confidence) — https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/sdks/v3/guides/swapping/quoting · keywords: Rebalance execution swap zap quoting slippage and MEV on Base
- [statement] Aero describes an MEV-tax module that increases the pool’s extra swap fee when the transaction priority fee exceeds a threshold. The same source says deployment will be gradual; applicability to a particular pool must be checked rather than assumed. Consequently, raising a priority fee can affect swap economics where that module is active. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://aero.xyz/llms-full.txt · keywords: Rebalance execution swap zap quoting slippage and MEV on Base

## Facts and statements

- [statement] A rebalance swap must target the token ratio required by the new liquidity position, and the swap itself can change that ratio. Uniswap documents atomic swap-and-add execution; Revert cautions that aggregator execution and concurrent swaps can still leave tokens after minting, which its implementation returns to the owner. Atomic execution should not be interpreted as a guarantee of zero dust. (medium confidence) — https://docs.uniswap.org/sdk/v3/guides/liquidity/swap-and-add · keywords: Rebalance execution swap zap quoting slippage and MEV on Base · also: https://docs.revert.finance/revert/auto-range
- [statement] Uniswap’s swap-and-add guide configures the leftover-dust recipient, slippageTolerance and deadline in swap options, and uses tokenId to identify the existing position. Treat this as a documented Uniswap integration pattern; direct compatibility with Aero routers is not established here. (low confidence) — https://docs.uniswap.org/sdk/v3/guides/liquidity/swap-and-add · keywords: Rebalance execution swap zap quoting slippage and MEV on Base
- [statement] Uniswap documents quoteExactInputSingle and quoteExactOutputSingle for one pool, and quoteExactInput and quoteExactOutput for multiple pools. Exact-input quotes solve for output; exact-output quotes solve for required input. (low confidence) — https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/sdks/v3/guides/swapping/quoting · keywords: Rebalance execution swap zap quoting slippage and MEV on Base
- [statement] Execution safeguards need to cover both swapping and liquidity placement: Krystal exposes separate Pool Slippage and Swap Slippage controls that can revert a transaction; Revert describes a maximum-price-impact threshold including pool fee, price impact and possible slippage, plus a pool-TWAP cross-check against price manipulation. These vendor mechanisms have different semantics and should not be treated as interchangeable settings. (medium confidence) — https://docs.krystal.app/products/liquidity-management/lp-management/lp-transactions/auto-rebalance · keywords: Rebalance execution swap zap quoting slippage and MEV on Base · also: https://docs.revert.finance/revert/auto-range
- [statement] Flashbots Protect’s overview describes protection for transactions on Ethereum and submission through rpc.flashbots.net/fast. That page alone does not establish a Base-compatible private submission route, so an LP bot should not infer Base support from the Flashbots name. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://docs.flashbots.net/flashbots-protect/overview · keywords: Rebalance execution swap zap quoting slippage and MEV on Base
- [statement] Base’s documentation gives conflicting deployment status: the Flashblocks reference calls Denim deprecation planned and not finalized, while the November 5, 2026 Base Engineering announcement says Denim is live and Flashblocks streams and pending preconfirmation state are retired. Preserve this as an attributed status conflict; confirm the target RPC’s deployed behavior before choosing Flashblocks-specific quoting or subscription semantics. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://docs.base.org/specifications/flashblocks · keywords: Rebalance execution swap zap quoting slippage and MEV on Base · also: https://www.base.org/blog/denim
- [statement] Private-mempool sandwich findings depend on the measurement scope. How to Serve Your Sandwich reports strong execution constraints and limits its analysis to same-block patterns, acknowledging possible cross-block attacks. No Place to Hide reports Base attacks associated with an RPC leak and predictable victim behavior, including wider and cross-block patterns. These attributed results do not justify a blanket guarantee that Base private submission prevents sandwiching. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19570 · keywords: Rebalance execution swap zap quoting slippage and MEV on Base · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28115
- [statement] Base’s Denim announcement distinguishes fast inclusion from finality: a block becomes safe after its batch is posted to Ethereum and final after Ethereum finalizes that batch. A fast receipt alone therefore does not establish final settlement of a rebalance. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://www.base.org/blog/denim · keywords: Rebalance execution swap zap quoting slippage and MEV on Base
